title: Novus Finance - POC scoping: workload modeling
next_steps: Sasha to send POC pricing and draft SOW by 2025-08-22
Miguel to schedule benchmark run with Novus sample corpus and provide run template by 2025-08-25
Novus to share representative traffic CSV and 1 week of telemetry by 2025-08-23

action_items: Sasha Nguyen - Share POC pricing and draft SOW - 2025-08-22
Miguel Ortiz - Provide benchmark run template and infra checklist - 2025-08-25

summary: AE+SE aligned with Novus on POC success criteria focused on latency SLOs, cost per inference, and throughput. Main work: collect representative traffic (QPS, concurrency, token distributions), run automated benchmarks against target models, and validate Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs. Timeline: share SOW/pricing, schedule benchmark kickoff, 2-week run, then evaluation meeting.
topics: Success criteria: latency SLO, throughput, cost per request, accuracy/regression limits
Workload characterization: QPS, concurrency, peak vs steady, input/output token distributions
Benchmark plan: sample corpus, models to test, quantization profiles, batching and caching configs
Deployment modes: hosted API vs dedicated pools vs private VPC
Timelines and next steps for POC run and acceptance criteria
transcript:
[00:00] Sasha Nguyen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll run about 45 minutes, go over what you need for the POC and then plan the benchmarks. 
[00:12] Priya Shah: Thanks Sasha. Appreciate it. We want to validate whether Redwood can meet our latency and cost targets for our fraud-alerting assistant. 
[00:20] Miguel Ortiz: Cool. Maybe quick intros? I'm Miguel, I'm an SE on infra/benchmarks. 
[00:26] Daniel Park: Daniel here, ML Eng, owns the model infra and the traffic shaping. 
[00:31] Rohit Mehta: Rohit, SRE, I handle networking and deployments. 
[00:35] Karen Li: Karen, Product, mainly tracking success criteria. 
[00:39] Sasha Nguyen: Great. So the ask from your email: workload modeling  QPS and concurrency, input/ output token shapes, success criteria, and timeline. Is that accurate? 
[00:48] Priya Shah: Yes. We get spikes from user behavior at month-end and around promotions. Baseline is about 5 QPS steady with spikes to ~70 QPS for short windows, concurrency around 40 at peaks. Those numbers are ballpark. 
[01:05] Miguel Ortiz: Okay ballpark is good to start. Two questions  is the 5 QPS steady per region or global? And what percent of requests are short (<=32 tokens) vs long (200-500 tokens)? 
[01:20] Daniel Park: That's global. Per region, US-east is ~60% of traffic. Token distribution: about 70% short (user prompt only), 20% medium (100-200 tokens), 10% long (300-600) because of combination with context/history. Output tokens vary: most responses 20-80 tokens, but some policy summaries generate 400+ tokens. 
[01:42] Sasha Nguyen: Good detail. For benchmarking we need a representative sample CSV: timestamp, input_tokens, output_tokens, model_variant, any special flags. Will that be feasible? 
[01:52] Daniel Park: Yes we can extract that. We'll sanitize PII. 
[01:56] Rohit Mehta: On networking  we'll likely want a private deployment but open to dedicated in Redwood cloud first to reduce complexity. We have strict firewall rules and will need to know IP ranges. 
[02:08] Miguel Ortiz: Noted. For the private option we'll need VPC peering details; for dedicated hosted we can run in our account or Redwood-managed reserved GPUs. 
[02:18] Karen Li: Success criteria from product side: 95th pct latency under 400ms for short prompts, under 1.2s for medium, and cost per 1k inference less than $X (we'll share target). Also model output quality shouldn't degrade more than 2% on our eval set. 
[02:37] Sasha Nguyen: Perfect  that gives us SLOs. On the cost target: we'll map per-token cost with different batch sizes and quant profiles. We'll test FP16, int8, and 4-bit where feasible. 
[02:48] Daniel Park: For our models we're currently using an open 13B variant and sometimes a 33B for heavy summarization. We care about memory footprint and latency. 
[02:58] Miguel Ortiz: For workload sizing, key metrics we'll model: steady QPS, peak QPS, concurrency (how many simultaneous KV cache warm requests), mean/median/95/99 latencies by token length, and token per request distributions. We'll create a traffic generator that replays the CSV with adjustable QPS and concurrency. 
[03:18] Priya Shah: One question  do you simulate user think-time and inter-arrival distributions? We have bursts that are not uniform. 
[03:24] Miguel Ortiz: Yes we can parameterize Poisson and heavy-tailed bursts; we also support replaying exact timestamps for determinism. 
[03:32] Sasha Nguyen: For benchmarks we'll provide a template; we'll run an initial hosted test to get baseline then run in dedicated and optionally private. Our typical POC runs are 2-3 weeks: 1 week setup/data, 1 week run/iterate, final week evaluate and prepare findings. 
[03:50] Daniel Park: That aligns. Are you going to run the GPU-based continuous batching? Our concern is that batching can hurt tail latency. 
[03:58] Miguel Ortiz: Right  Redwood runtime supports workload-aware batching with latency SLOs: we can cap batch windows and fall back to smaller batches for short prompts. We'll test different batching policies and measure p95/p99. 
[04:12] Karen Li: For the long responses that are >300 tokens, are you recommending streaming? 
[04:16] Miguel Ortiz: Yes streaming reduces perceived latency; but it doesn't reduce total compute. We'll show both token-by-token latency and end-to-end completion time. 
[04:26] Priya Shah: How do we capture cold-start vs warmed KV cache performance? Many of our requests reuse conversation history. 
[04:33] Miguel Ortiz: We'll run both cold and warm scenarios. For warm runs we pre-load KV cache and run a mix reflective of your % of returned users. For cold starts we'll simulate new sessions. 
[04:43] Sasha Nguyen: Any regulatory requirements we should flag? Priya? 
[04:47] Priya Shah: SOC2 is required, plus we need audit logs and KMS integration for private pilot. Also data retention policies, and we prefer customer-managed KMS. 
[04:57] Sasha Nguyen: Redwood supports SOC2, SSO/SAML, and KMS integrations. We'll share security docs. 
[05:02] Rohit Mehta: For the private env, what about GPU types? We have a preference for A100-ish performance; if you recommend cheaper cards we'll need to see benchmark delta. 
[05:12] Miguel Ortiz: We'll capture model-memory and throughput curves across A100 and H100 equivalents and show cost-per-inference tradeoffs. We sometimes run quantized int8 on cheaper hardware, but H100 gives much better latency at large batch sizes. 
[05:24] Daniel Park: For concurrency modeling: our service parallelizes to 8 worker threads per instance; what's the mapping to Redwood worker model? 
[05:31] Miguel Ortiz: In Redwood, a worker process typically handles a set of request lanes and a KV cache instance. For concurrency we map to number of concurrent request slots per GPU (e.g., 4-16 depending on model and fp). We'll produce recommended pool sizes based on your peak concurrency and desired SLOs. 
[05:47] Sasha Nguyen: Regarding benchmarks: the plan is  Novus provides dataset + expected SLOs. Redwood runs initial hosted baseline (3 model variants: 13B fp16, 13B int8, 33B fp16) with 2 traffic profiles (steady and burst). We'll measure p50/p95/p99, throughput, and cost per 1k tokens. Then we iterate on batching/ caching and produce a report. 
[06:10] Karen Li: What's acceptance criteria for POC success? 
[06:13] Sasha Nguyen: We propose: (1) Meet latency SLOs for 95th percentile for short/medium ranges, (2) Cost per 1k inference within acceptable threshold (you'll provide target), (3) No functional regressions on your eval set (<=2% drop), (4) Implementation/runbook for your infra. 
[06:29] Priya Shah: That seems reasonable. If you meet those, we'll consider expanding to dedicated reserved capacity. 
[06:35] Miguel Ortiz: One operational note  to model traffic accurately we need your histogram of input/output tokens. If you can't share raw logs, a sampled histogram is fine. 
[06:45] Daniel Park: We'll extract a 7-day sample and produce histogram buckets (0-32, 33-100, 101-200, 201-400, 400+). 
[06:54] Sasha Nguyen: Great. For the benchmark run we'll also need a representative seed set of heavy summaries (maybe 50 records) to stress the 33B path. 
[07:02] Karen Li: I'll compile the eval set and quality metrics; we'll aim to keep the evaluation script simple  accuracy/ROUGE/and a custom fraud-detection precision metric. 
[07:14] Miguel Ortiz: On measuring cost, we'll instrument token counts and GPU utilization and map to estimated unit cost; for hosted runs we'll provide actual billed preview; for dedicated we'll show modeled costs per GPU hour. 
[07:27] Rohit Mehta: Network egress and VPC peering costs also matter. We'll need to know any persistent IPs or egress patterns. 
[07:34] Miguel Ortiz: We'll include network cost modeling as a line item. 
[07:37] Priya Shah: Any idea on how long a full benchmark run takes? 
[07:40] Miguel Ortiz: Depends on sample size. For a 1 million request replay at steady 5 QPS, it's ~2.3 days. For bursts, we can compress by parallelizing across multiple workers to simulate same load faster, but we prefer realistic timing for cache behavior. For POC we'll run smaller runs (100k requests) across the key profiles which takes a few hours to a day. 
[08:01] Daniel Park: If we parallelize we lose KV cache fidelity though. 
[08:04] Miguel Ortiz: Correct  we'll do both: replay for cache fidelity and parallel runs to stress throughput. 
[08:10] Sasha Nguyen: Let's talk deliverables and timeline: Sasha sends SOW/pricing by Fri (2025-08-22). Novus shares traffic CSV and eval set by Sat (2025-08-23). Redwood schedules benchmark kickoff Wed (2025-08-27). Benchmark runs week of 2025-09-01. Results and findings meeting target 2025-09-12. 
[08:32] Priya Shah: That timeline looks good. 
[08:36] Karen Li: A couple of nitty gritty  how will you measure tail latency for streaming responses? Do you measure time-to-first-byte and time-to-last-byte? 
[08:44] Miguel Ortiz: We measure both TTFB and completion time; for streaming we capture first chunk latency and completion latency and token inter-arrival times. 
[08:52] Daniel Park: For the model variants  can Redwood test different quantization profiles on the same hardware? We want to know if int8 yields similar output quality for our evals. 
[08:59] Miguel Ortiz: Yes, we'll test int8 and 4-bit where supported; we'll run quality diffs against your eval script and report regression numbers. 
[09:09] Rohit Mehta: If we do a private pilot, what's the onboarding time for your private control plane? 
[09:14] Sasha Nguyen: Typically 2-4 weeks to stand up the control plane + networking, depending on approvals. The dedicated reserved capacity path is faster (1-2 weeks) since it's pre-provisioned. 
[09:24] Priya Shah: Good to know. Any blockers from our side besides traffic and eval set? 
[09:28] Sasha Nguyen: Mostly network approvals for private, and credentials to access the telemetry. We'll send a checklist. 
[09:33] Miguel Ortiz: I'll also attach a minimal benchmark infra checklist: firewall rules, seed IP ranges, sample payload format, and expected model artifacts. 
[09:42] Karen Li: On contract  will we sign an NDA or will the SOW include data handling terms? 
[09:46] Sasha Nguyen: We'll include a short NDA clause in the SOW and reference security addendum. If you need enterprise terms, we'll loop in legal. 
[09:53] Daniel Park: One more technical  do you support KV cache persistence across restarts? For lower latency on resumed sessions. 
[09:58] Miguel Ortiz: We support cached checkpoints and warmup scripts; persistent caches are possible with the private deployment. For hosted/dedicated we manage ephemeral caches but we can preload. 
[10:08] Priya Shah: Ok. That covers my questions. 
[10:11] Sasha Nguyen: To recap next steps: we'll share SOW/pricing and the benchmark template; Novus will share traffic CSV and eval set; we'll schedule the kickoff. We'll run baseline hosted tests, then iterate on configs, and produce final report. 
[10:24] Priya Shah: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the kickoff. 
[10:28] Sasha Nguyen: Thanks all. We'll follow up with calendar invites and artifacts (Deck: https://redwood.app/shared/poc-deck and Benchmark template: https://redwood.app/shared/bench-template). End call.
